checks.detail: Swept V continuously 0.000-1.300 in 0.005 steps against crime/witness.js::isWitness at 2.0 m with clear LOS. Exactly three outcomes and two edges: below V_min 0.100 not a witness (0 g); 0.100-0.295 witness but NOT identified (118 g); >= identified_at_V 0.300 identified (294 g). 118 = Math.round(294 x 0.4), the partial_report multiplier. The dark arm's measured V of 0.2720 sits correctly between the two. CONTROL: a deliberately continuous grader over the same sweep produces 200 edges, so the sweep can see a slope and the shipped model genuinely has none — it is a clean step, not a fitted curve or a coincidence.

Classified all 16 occurrences of `identified` in game/src. Exactly ONE changes a decision: sim/crime/state.js:154, `const partial = !witnessRec.identified || witnessRec.kind === 'hearing'` — the 0.4x bounty multiplier. stepGuards() derives its band from guardBandNow(), which reads crime.bounty.imperial plus the player's race and standing and nothing else, so a guard cannot distinguish one 294 g identified bounty from two 118 g unidentified ones plus 58 g. justice.json's own witness.unidentified_effect promises three further consequences — 'bounty lands as person or persons unknown; GUARDS DO NOT APPROACH YOU FOR IT, but it counts toward the settlement's alarm state and toward RI-STL01 §7's S-4 zone memory' — and NONE of the three is implemented: the report log writes attributed:null and nothing consults it, there is no settlement alarm state, and there is no path from an unattributed report to ZoneMemory. Being SUSPECTED and being WANTED are the same state at different magnitudes.

A genuine and well-derived addition. The world's ~1,700 authored schedule rows take eight activity values and none of them is sleep, so before this nothing in the build could tell a resident in bed from a resident in the doorway and a 03:00 burglary was watched by every resident of the house with a full cone. asleepInWorld(sim,npc) reads `home` between 23:00 and 06:00 off the schedule the world already publishes rather than authoring a second source of truth. The round's four-witness staging holds up: same position and distance as the awake arm, opposite outcome.

Round 2's blocking gap is half closed and no further. guard_legion's gold_price went 0 -> 300, which is above the round-2 verdict's stated >= 200 g floor and is a real improvement. The other two legs are untouched and correctly declared untouched: the GOLD ground's disposition floor is shared by every parleying NPC in the data, and guard_legion's ai 'hold_ground' still means combat/enemy.js scripts nothing for it, so a band-3 attack-on-sight guard still cannot swing. Both files are owned elsewhere and were under concurrent edit; documenting rather than half-fixing was the right call.

The rule-11 caveat is printed in the tool's own output. I could not find a wrong row among the 116.

THE ONE IT MISSED. The tool's FILES list has seven entries; game/data/{stealth,crime} holds eight. The absentee is game/data/stealth/search.json, read as this.d.search in six places in sim/stealth/system.js and unambiguously W1-15's. All 28 of its parameters come back 'read by name', which is the point: this is rule 11 running in the direction nobody checks, where a name census proves a read LIVE that isn't. search.js:85 reads s1.max_cover_volumes to slice a list that is always empty because coverVolumes has only a harness producer. Round 2 had already graded the model that file configures — plausibleSet, S-1 — at coupling 0.0. The one W1-15 data file with a verdict-confirmed dead consumer is the one the census excluded.

Re-ran tools/harness/w1-15-r3-deletefix.mjs independently: 5/5. The teardown BITES rather than silently running the positive arm — the cut arm returns 0 world sources and L flat at 0.7500 (spread 0) at noon and 0.0900 at 03:00, theft null, registry 0 -> 0, inventory row stolen:false/owner:null. The stager throws unless each cut string occurs exactly once and all three still do at 9126e02. DTF-CTL (an uncut copy) reproduces the working tree, so the staging is not the variable. The round's report that its first DTF-LAMP-OLD run FAILED because it hardcoded clear-weather sky values against an overcast default is exactly the evidence rule 4 asks for.

The lamp fix has TWO edit sites and the round cuts both as ONE arm, so rule 6's third shape (two guards for one defect) was invisible to it and 'say which you have' could not be satisfied. I crossed them on four staged copies. 00 shipped: 8 sources, ambient 0.04, L 0.2988-1.0000, spread 0.7012. 10 call-site cut only: 0 sources, flat 0.7500, 0.0900 at 03:00. 01 ambient cut only: 8 sources, ambient 0.75, L FLAT AT 1.0000, spread 0. 11 both cut: byte-identical to 10. VERDICT: neither an inert fix nor two-guards-for-one-defect — two INDEPENDENT sites, each individually sufficient, so the round's arm is sound but over-broad. AND THE FINDING ONLY A 2x2 PRODUCES: arm 01 shows the lamps ALONE do not make the room discriminate — keep them and restore the old ambient and the room is as flat as before, just clamped at the other end. What bought the 0.7012 spread was the 0.75 -> 0.04 ambient decision, which §1 shows is calibrated on a windowless cellar that does not exist in this data.

L enters exactly one place — visibilityAt's light term — and V feeds the alert meter. Neither appears in any damage or hit-resolution path. Snuffing a lamp changes WHEN an enemy notices you (40 -> 80 frames), never WHETHER an attack lands.

Examined rather than waved. tools/world/build-unique-property.mjs:90 sets value = band[0] + (hashStr(u.id) % range) — a BUILD-TIME, deterministic, permanently stable price derived from the item's own id and banded by interior kind. No runtime table, no roll, no drop; every value is fixed and inspectable in the data forever, and the rows describe objects a human authored. That is not procedural loot. It IS a content debt — a hash cannot tell a priceless heirloom from a chipped bowl, and 72 objects now carry prices nobody wrote — and it is filed under other_gaps because it is exactly the practice that becomes an AR-2 failure if it spreads to the other 1,878.
getStealthState().hud_elements remains 0 across every run recorded here. The lamps added no indicator, no visibility gem and no objective marker; the only surface a player reads is the world itself.

NEW THIS ROUND and the piece's best seam crossing. An authored interior lamp — a world object placed by a settlement generator — now writes into the alert meter combat/enemy.js reads. Snuff it and an enemy's time-to-aggro doubles, 40 frames to 80, at the same distance with the same line of sight. Morrowind's world reaching into the Souls fight through a physical object you can act on.

Carried from round 2 and re-read at this commit: guardBandNow() computes JUS.thresholds from the player's race and faction standing, so an imperial bounty of 3,000 makes a militiaman attack a Naga on sight and merely greet an Imperial. The world's social position deciding whether a fight starts.

score.note: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE NUMBER. Round 2 scored 3.0 by MEAN; this critic was briefed to score MIN-OVER-AXES and scores 0.0. THE AGGREGATION CHANGED — 3.0 -> 0.0 IS NOT A REGRESSION SIGNAL. The like-for-like comparison is mean 3.0 -> 2.7, and the entire 0.3 is RI-STL02 moving 4 -> 2 because round 2 scored its fencing axis 8 on refusal lines this round measured unreachable in play. The min itself is RI-STL01's, and it is carried by two axes W1-15 owns and did not close: S-1's search plan (coverVolumes has only a harness producer — the SAME defect shape this round fixed for the lamps) and the trespass ladder (p.zone has no producer at all). Both are 0 by ARBITRATION §3's own rule that an unconsumed model is unmeasurable => 0. Meanwhile the light axis went 0 -> 8 and is the largest single consumption gain in this piece's history: 827 authored lamps that no part of the detection model had ever been told about now decide when an enemy notices you. A reader who takes 0.0 as 'nothing works' will be wrong about this round in both directions.

biggest_gap.what: Engine.fenceQuote() (game/src/engine.js:8541) hands sim/stealth/theft.js::willBuy() a stub world — `const world = { npcById: () => null, dispositionBetween: () => 0 }`. willBuy() resolves an owner's settlement and faction through npcById and the friend-of-the-owner test through dispositionBetween, so for any object owned by a PERSON all four of its refusal branches are unreachable. Measured live at 9126e02: an object owned by npc:archon-legionary-13 of archon is bought by fence.archon.salvage — archon's own fence — at 15 g, EXACTLY the price it pays for a clean-item control, and LESS than three out-of-town fences pay (16, 17, 17 g). 1,787 of 1,950 property objects (91.6%) are affected; the 123 faction:- and 40 settlement:-owned rows do reach the refusals, because willBuy() parses those out of the owner string with a regex needing no npcById. The control separates cleanly: the identical willBuy() call with a real npcById over game/data/npcs/ returns {buys:false, reason:'same_settlement'} with an authored refusal line naming the victim.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This piece exists to make theft have geography and memory — witnesses who saw you, guards who know things, factions who care, consequences that persist. All of that is built, correct and measured, and every gram of it is discharged at the point of sale by a fence who will buy you your victim's own furniture at the honest-goods price, in the victim's own town, while the fence three towns away pays more. From the player's chair, stealing has no map: it is strictly optimal to rob the house next door and sell to the man who drinks with the owner, and the refusal lines somebody wrote for exactly that moment — 'That belongs to Ahnassi Dark-Water of terraces. I drink with Ahnassi Dark-Water of terraces. Take it elsewhere.' — can never be spoken. It also means round 2 scored two axes (ownership enforcement 8, fencing 8) partly on authored text that could not run, so this is a correction to the record as well as a defect. And it is the same failure this round's own headline is about, one system over: a model computed correctly, sitting behind a stubbed accessor, consumed by nothing.

remedy.action: In Engine.fenceQuote() (game/src/engine.js:8541) replace the stub world with a real one: npcById resolving `npc:<id>` against this.data.npcs — the 347-record table the Engine already holds and already walks in populateSettlement() — and dispositionBetween reading the disposition model W1-18 owns, or, if that is not yet addressable, an explicit `() => 0` carrying a why_not note so the friend_of_the_owner branch is DECLARED dead rather than silently so. Then add a crime-audit assertion that quotes the same stolen object at the owner's local fence and at an out-of-town fence and REQUIRES THEM TO DIFFER — the current FNC-4 checks the authored refusal lines exist and never checks they can fire. Budget a regression pass: this moves existing stl-probe and crime-audit fencing assertions, which is exactly why the round correctly declined to attempt it without a browser.

other_gaps.what: `identified` has exactly one decision-changing reader in game/src (crime/state.js:154's 0.4x bounty multiplier). justice.json's own witness.unidentified_effect promises that guards do not approach you for an unattributed bounty, that it feeds a settlement alarm state, and that it feeds RI-STL01 §7's S-4 zone memory. None of the three exists: the report log writes attributed:null and nothing consults it, there is no settlement alarm state, and there is no path to ZoneMemory.
other_gaps.why_it_matters: Being suspected and being wanted are supposed to be different states and the data file says so. In the running build they are the same state at different magnitudes, so the beautiful thing the lamps just made possible — you were seen and not recognised — buys the player nothing but a smaller number.
other_gaps.remedy: Carry `attributed` on the bounty ledger rather than only in the log line, and make guardBandNow() read the ATTRIBUTED share of the bounty rather than the total. An unattributed 3,000 g should leave a guard at band 1 while raising the settlement's suspicion of everyone.

other_gaps.what: build-unique-property.mjs:90 prices the 72 newly wired unique items as band[0] + (hashStr(id) % range), banded by interior_kind. Deterministic, build-time, permanently stable and inspectable — not procedural loot and not an AR-2 failure — but a hash cannot tell a priceless heirloom from a chipped bowl, and 72 named objects now carry prices nobody wrote.
other_gaps.why_it_matters: This is the practice that becomes an AR-2 failure if it spreads to the other 1,878 objects. Named now, while it is 72.
other_gaps.remedy: Author values for the 72, or narrow the bands per interior_kind until the hash cannot produce an absurd price for a named object.

corpus_extended.what: RI-STL01 §3 gives L for 'a torchlit interior' and 'unlit' and says nothing about a WINDOW, and RI-CRM01 §2's witness predicate gives `identified` a threshold and no consequence beyond the bounty multiplier. Both gaps were hit head-on this round: 112 of 115 shipped interiors are drawn with windows the light model cannot represent, and justice.json had to invent `unidentified_effect` in prose because no reference item says what being unrecognised DOES.
corpus_extended.proposed: Two additions, neither filed as an amendment because both are the builder-side of a corpus silence rather than a contradiction in it. (1) RI-STL01 §3 should carry a daylight-through-an-opening row, so an indoor ambient is a function of the room's own openings rather than a single constant chosen between 'sky' and 'cellar'. (2) RI-CRM01 §2 should say what a settlement does with an unattributed bounty — the difference between SUSPECTED and WANTED is the texture the whole system is for, and at present it is a 0.4x multiplier with a prose note attached.
corpus_extended.status: proposed by this critic, not ruled
